assertion_analysis.failure_condition: test_carrier_key_ignores_computed_wall_bits_but_covers_inputs asserts fixture_digest(rounded) == fixture_digest(identity) after perturbing only wall_content.sha256; it fails if the digests stop stripping wall_content. The negative control (negative_control_final.log) reinstates that behaviour by neutering _defining_identity and the assertion reddens (3 failed, EXIT=1). Independent of any value the test passes in.

The loop asserts each defining input (analytic_case, requested_cells, major_radius_m, builder_revision, builder) changes the digest; it fails if _defining_identity over-strips any of them. It is sensitive to over-stripping across the listed keys.

test_second_device_loads_without_publishing_again asserts json.loads(loaded.attrs['semantic_identity']) == rounded and cache_key == reader.key; it fails if load() stops rewriting the stored defining identity back to the device-local identity, which is the contract the fixture owner's own validation depends on.

The repointed assertion computes canonical from certificate_fixtures._defining_identity(identity) and compares sha256(canonical) to fixture_digest(identity); both sides route through the module's own private helper, so it reddens if fixture_digest stops calling _defining_identity but NOT if _defining_identity itself over-strips a defining input — the very regression the node introduced. See finding.

findings.text: follow-on: the pre-existing digest assertion was repointed onto the module's own private helper. It now computes canonical = json.dumps(certificate_fixtures._defining_identity(identity)) (line 241) and compares it to certificate_fixtures.fixture_digest(identity) (line 246), so both sides move together through _defining_identity. It still catches fixture_digest dropping the helper, but it can no longer catch _defining_identity over-stripping a defining input (e.g. removing requested_cells or support_arm), which is exactly the failure mode this node's change introduces; that guard survives only in the new scripts/prototypes/support/test_certificate_fixtures.py:43.

follow-on: _defining_identity strips the two analytic binary64 digests only when 'machine_semantic_key' is present, keyed on an unrelated marker rather than on the keys being removed. A carrier-shaped identity that carried analytic_state_sha256_binary64 would silently retain a device-rounded digest in its address, and the done_when claim that no identity hashes a device-rounded computed array would then be false by convention rather than by construction. Not reachable today because only the exterior identity carries those keys.

follow-on: the paired arms the manifest records as baseline_suite/after_suite (identity_suite_arm.sh) cover only tests/test_current_book_fragments... tests/test_current_book_fragments.py and scripts/prototypes/support/test_certificate_fixtures.py, while done_when (3) names four paths.
